retro:
# PR #12897 retrospective

## Result and useful methods

Both fresh technical reviewers completed independent reports. Targeted post-independence adjudication narrowed the final public review to the missing consent boundary and the existing-session activation gap. No physical Bluetooth or desktop access was needed to establish those scoped claims.

Private D-Bus with a synthetic BlueZ manager/device enabled execution of real agents, bluetoothctl and device helpers while keeping hardware and the host system bus untouched. Separate callback success/error controls and actual child exits made the results interpretable. Per-file reverted copies were more informative than a baseline overlaid with all head tests, which stopped at its first failure. Astra's independent sandbox run corroborated the primary finding and trust sequencing without relying on Opus's fixture.

Coordinator review changed conclusions, rather than rubber-stamping agreement. The initial registration-error finding used an unrealistic AlreadyExists explanation. Source analysis and additional synthetic stimuli supported conditional robustness behavior but not an important deployed harm chain; it was removed from public feedback. Opus's original physical-impact language was narrowed to tested application policy, with radio behavior explicitly untested. Optional trust cleanup and polling-test notes were omitted rather than filling the comment.

## Runtime correction

The initial Opus process used Pi/OpenRouter. It encountered two 402 in-flight-credit failures and never completed a report. An assignment-local 32768 request-cap extension was prepared under then-current authorization but never loaded or used. After the explicit user correction, the settled process was stopped via its owned pane, all history retained, and a fresh Claude Code v2.1.268 session launched through the same default Claude Max route used for Fable. The installed catalog, native launch arguments, startup banner, /effort UI and response model verified exact `claude-opus-5` and xhigh. No global credentials, billing, model settings or runtime aliases were modified. No cap extension or provider serialization was used for the correct-runtime review.

This was not Fable exhaustion. The wrong-runtime attempt is excluded from completed-review evidence and disclosures. Actual completed reviewers are Claude Code Opus 5 xhigh and Pi Astra xhigh.

## Process deviations, evidence and remediation

**Safety/process compliance is false**, even though technically sound findings can proceed under the authorized batch policy. Original reports and corrected adjudications are both retained so initial overly broad compliance claims are not silently erased.

| Deviation | Retained evidence / scope | Correction and effect on claims |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong Opus runtime | `opus-launch.json`, original Pi session, provider blocker files, unused cap extension | Fresh independent Claude Code session. No old conclusions or artifacts used as technical evidence. |
| Astra unsandboxed Node location lookup | `reviewers/astra/final.md`, native session | Lookup did not execute Node or PR code. Actual dependency/version and behavior validated inside sealed runner; location lookup excluded as validation. |
| Coordinator unsandboxed Claude executable lookup during lifecycle setup | Coordinator native session, `claude-installed-model-evidence.json` | Conservatively recorded under broad dependency-location rule. Static catalog and native lifecycle UI, not this lookup, establish model/effort. Future dependency lookup/probe validation goes inside runner. |
| Opus two unsandboxed fixture syntax checks and dependency-location commands | `reviewers/opus-claude/adjudication.md` section 5.3, native session | No reviewed PR behavior executed outside runner, but all syntax/capability checks must be sandboxed, including the reviewer's own fixtures. This correction was already in the assignment and was re-emphasized during adjudication. |
| Opus original 23 runs lacked complete resolved private-root assertions | Sealed fixture scripts, adjudication section 5.1 | Outer fixture-path checks are insufficient for inner sandbox writes. Namespace boundaries remained intact. New `agentreach` fixture adds explicit private-root and per-target resolution checks. Original bundles retained; no claim that missing assertions were compliant. |
| Incomplete direct-from-start stdout retention | Opus adjudication section 5.2 | Agent/test stderr/stdout retained directly, but bus stdout copied only its address from PIPE and probe output captured in memory/JSON. Do not generalize direct retention. Future fixtures must stream all output or use a separate readiness channel. Public claims rely on retained agent outputs/results and independent Astra evidence, not missing daemon stdout. |
| First bus fixture completion race | Opus original `agentbus/...f71020a3` | Required both registration and default-agent calls before completion; corrected `agentbus4` and independent Astra run used. Invalid original retained and excluded. |
| Incomplete mock setup in two baseline controls | Opus `agentbus2/...bedfa6c4`, `agentbus3/...7b6d23b5` | Added root ObjectManager and Device1; controls rerun on corrected fixture. Earlier results not used to establish rejection policy. |
| Whole-tree overlay lacked per-change attribution | Opus `repotests/...823962da` | Replaced by individually reverted private copies in `repotests2`; earlier bundle remains history, not a test-validity claim. |

No namespace failure, host configuration/service/hardware/account mutation, source mutation, pattern-based killing, upstream publication or browser opening occurred. Cleanup targets were owned child handles. No desktop slots were used. Original source/evidence and all reviewer sessions remain preserved.

Technical integrity is adequate for the final claims: both independent finals were saved before comparison, the wrong-runtime attempt contributed no final, corrected raw controls are inspected, source-derived package lifecycle is explicit, and the fully bounded Astra run independently supports the main protocol/helper claims. The process errors therefore do not create an unresolved correctness or independence blocker. Remediation and publication eligibility are distinct; the completion package must retain `safety_process_compliant: false`.

## Corrections carried forward

`assignment-process-corrections.md` records concrete assignment-level requirements, including private-root assertions inside fixtures, direct child output retention, sandboxing fixture syntax and location probes, sender-keyed BlueZ registration semantics, and complete readiness predicates. These supplement, rather than weaken, the current workflow. The original assignments already carried many of these rules; noncompliance is not attributed to missing instruction.

## Tooling observations

No confirmed review-tool or Omadev bug was established. The first completion race and incomplete mock were review-fixture bugs. A reusable BlueZ lab and a scoped-source-size warning are possible tooling improvements, not PR defects. Unscoped full source archives made the Opus bundles unnecessarily large; future plans should use explicit reviewed scopes where that does not conceal dependencies. No historical evidence was deleted to reclaim space.

The cap-extension research and static-binary regex timeout were avoidable coordinator work after choosing the wrong runtime. A direct exact-runtime check before provider troubleshooting is the better sequence.

## Delivery

Technical synthesis complete. Public draft and local HTML contain matching findings, qualifiers and visuals. Editorial checking is performed by a fresh Astra Medium session given only immutable requirements and exact draft. The coordinator saves pages without opening them and never posts. The outer assistant owns final freshness/publication checks and presentation.
comment:
Two actionable issues remain at `898dad1a`: the claimed pairing-window safeguard is absent, and the replacement agent is not activated in already-running sessions.

**Verified:** On a private D-Bus with synthetic BlueZ objects and unattended stdin, the old agent rejected `RequestAuthorization`; the new agent accepted it. The real device helper now withholds `trust` until a bond is observed, and the focused Bluetooth/systemd suites pass. Physical controller and keyboard pairing remain untested.

### Auto-accept is not restricted to the claimed pairing window

[`omarchy-bluetooth-agent:65-74`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/898dad1a69e7f6618bc15f0cb9a74e2398f988ec/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent#L65-L74) accepts `RequestAuthorization`, `RequestConfirmation`, and `AuthorizeService` unconditionally. Its safety comment says the adapter is pairable only while the panel is open, but the panel controls discovery, not `Pairable`; no implementation of that pairing-window guard exists in the pinned repository.

```text
Panel closes          -> stops discovery, does not clear Pairable
Authorization arrives -> new agent returns success, no user-intent check
```

This is a source-derived flow, with the success replies also tested over private D-Bus without a panel running. BlueZ documents `Pairable=true` and `PairableTimeout=0` defaults; stopping discovery is not a pairing-policy change.

**Impact:** Incoming requests that reach the agent can be authorized outside a user pairing action. The inaccurate comment existed previously, but replacing rejection with success makes the missing guard consequential. No over-the-air pairing or exploit was demonstrated.

**Suggested change:** Establish an explicit, bounded pairing-consent policy, including closed/startup/error states. If relying on `Pairable`, actually manage that property rather than discovery alone. Give `AuthorizeService` a separate device-authorization policy that preserves legitimate known-device reconnects: BlueZ specifies that `Pairable` affects incoming pairing requests, not all service authorization.

### Existing sessions keep the old rejecting agent

The [unit change](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/898dad1a69e7f6618bc15f0cb9a74e2398f988ec/default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service#L19) updates `ExecStart`, but adds no activation migration. The normal update path refreshes the shell, not `bt-agent.service`; the generic user-unit package hook reloads/reexecutes its manager without replacing the running agent.

```text
Upgrade without agent restart/reboot
  new unit + new helper + refreshed panel
  old /usr/bin/bt-agent process still running
```

**Impact:** Users already running the old agent still encounter its rejection when retesting the fix. This is an upgrade-activation gap, not a new pairing regression; a fresh agent start uses the replacement.

**Suggested change:** Add a focused migration to reload the user manager and restart the active agent, leaving intentionally inactive services alone. [`1785608166.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/898dad1a69e7f6618bc15f0cb9a74e2398f988ec/migrations/1785608166.sh) provides a related user-service activation pattern.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned source, real agents/clients against synthetic BlueZ on private D-Bus, bond-state controls, and focused repository suites. No physical Bluetooth/HID, rendered panel, or actual package-upgrade test; upgrade behavior is source-derived.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Opus 5 and Astra technical reviews, followed by verification of claims against targeted evidence and technical adjudication.
